results.title: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator protects neurons after ...
results.content: # Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator protects neurons after intracerebral hemorrhage through activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) shows neuroprotective effects in intracerebral hemorrhage models. It reduces neuronal damage, apoptosis, and autophagy by activating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway, suggesting a direct benefit beyond hematoma removal. * Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) is used in minimally invasive surgery for intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). * Potential contact with brain tissue necessitates safety and efficacy evaluation of tPA in ICH. * To investigate the direct neuroprotective effects of recombinant tPA in ICH. * Recombinant tPA improved neurological function and reduced damage, apoptosis, and autophagy in ICH mice. * Transcriptome analysis revealed tPA upregulates the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway. * Inhibitor studies confirmed the involvement of PI3K/Akt/mTOR and EGFR pathways. * Recombinant tPA exerts direct neuroprotective effects in ICH models. * The PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway activation is crucial for tPA's neuroprotective actions. * EGFR signaling is implicated in mediating tPA's effects on the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway.
